scope: Tracks completed relationship research so the same source question is not repeated without a new trigger.
reopenPolicy: Reopen a closed item only when a new primary source, a fixed historical version, a resolved endpoint identity, or a materially different relation claim becomes available.

entries.note: Brendan Eich author recollection supports Java-like syntax and platform positioning; scope is limited design reference, not succession or compatibility.
Brendan Eich author recollection supports Scheme-ish first-class functions; scope is limited to that design point.
Dart language specification supports browser/JavaScript compatibility and syntax choices; not general inheritance or compilation-target lineage.
Cython official About page explicitly calls Cython a superset of Python and names its C/C++ extensions.
C3 official compiler README explicitly names C2 as its inspiration.
Generic Assembly is not a single historical language; NASM/x86 documentation does not support a generic upstream design edge.
entries.reopenWhen: A concrete instruction set or assembler dialect and a specific historical design event are identified.

entries.note: W3C 1997 XSL proposal explicitly says “XSL is based on DSSSL,” but the fixed PLDB snapshot has no DSSSL endpoint, so no valid relationship can be written without a curated-record/external-endpoint mechanism.
entries.reopenWhen: A curated DSSSL record or an explicitly supported external endpoint is added to the catalogue model.

entries.note: Official Mojo material supports Python interoperability and compatibility, not a sufficiently explicit design-influence claim.
entries.reopenWhen: An official Mojo design history or specification explicitly names Python as a design source for a concrete feature.

entries.note: Reopens Batch 16: Chapel official overview now provides direct primary-source wording naming C++ as a primary influence; no inheritance or compatibility claim.
The current Objective-J/Cappuccino official entry point was not stably retrievable; the existing field is not upgraded from a third-party summary.
entries.reopenWhen: A stable official Objective-J source or fixed repository revision is available.

entries.note: BQN official homepage explicitly says it removes burdensome parts of the APL tradition while maintaining ideas that made APL/ APL\360 revolutionary; scope is design input, not source compatibility.

JSON official homepage explicitly says JSON is based on a subset of the JavaScript Programming Language Standard; scope is data-notation syntax/design, not executable JavaScript or runtime compatibility.
C3 official README describes C3 as an evolution retaining familiar C syntax and semantics and lists evolving C as a goal; scope is design input, not strict superset or source compatibility.
AssemblyScript official homepage says TypeScript-like and highlights similarity, but this batch found no explicit design-source statement sufficient to upgrade the field relation.
entries.reopenWhen: An official AssemblyScript design history or fixed source explicitly names TypeScript as a design input for concrete features.

entries.note: Stanford-hosted ALGOL W implementation report states the implemented language was based on Wirth/Hoare’s development work and points to that paper for historical background and goals. Scope is design/implementation input, not strict superset or source compatibility.
Wirth-family continuity and later Modula documentation were not treated as proof of a direct ALGOL 60 design edge; no qualifying direct statement was secured in this batch.
entries.reopenWhen: A Modula primary report or author account explicitly identifies a concrete ALGOL 60 design input.

entries.note: The official Oberon report is useful for Oberon’s own specification, but this batch did not obtain a direct ALGOL 60 design-source statement; intervening Modula history is not collapsed into a direct edge.
entries.reopenWhen: An Oberon or Wirth primary source explicitly identifies ALGOL 60 as a concrete design input rather than only a family background.

entries.note: The IBM SEQUEL 2 paper identity is present, but the batch could not obtain a stable readable primary copy that directly supports the SQL endpoint claim; the PLDB field remains unupgraded.
entries.reopenWhen: A stable IBM paper copy or fixed archival source explicitly connects SQL to the specific SEQUEL 2 version.

entries.note: Re-read Brendan Eich’s Popularity author account; response SHA matches the existing saved source. Explicit Self-ish singular prototypes support a limited prototype-object design input, not full Self semantics, succession or source compatibility.

Fixed Curry 0.9.0 report (2016-01-13), §5.5 footnote 10 and §7, explicitly adopts Haskell field-label description and monadic I/O. Version-specific design input; neither syntax similarity nor the KiCS2 Haskell back end establishes inheritance or whole-language compatibility.

McCarthy 1960 Functions and Forms explicitly adopts Church notation; author prehistory item c limits the mechanism. Supports function notation, not full lambda calculus implementation or runtime identity.

Fixed MLIR Rationale revision explicitly draws on LLVM IR ideas for low-level constructs; old standard dialect integer semantics and operation split provide concrete design scope. Excludes lowering, project affiliation, compatibility and LLVM PHI inheritance.

Official Civet Philosophy explicitly names design inputs; Reference gives CoffeeScript opt-in loop/compatibility options and LiveScript boolean-property shorthand. Limited design influence, not blanket source compatibility or runtime inheritance.

Official Civet Philosophy explicitly names design inputs; Reference gives CoffeeScript opt-in loop/compatibility options and LiveScript boolean-property shorthand. Limited design influence, not blanket source compatibility or runtime inheritance.
Official comparison documents intentional incompatibilities; snapshot supersetOf corrected to a scoped design input.
Author POPL 1997 summary explicitly calls Pizza a strict superset; limited to historical design, not modern Java or runtime certification.
CLtL2 explicitly calls Common Lisp a new dialect of Lisp; family identity, not strict superset or source compatibility.
CLtL2 explicitly calls Common Lisp a successor to MacLisp; multi-party standardization is not reduced to a single-line version.
CLtL2 says Common Lisp was influenced by Scheme to some extent; limited design input, not succession or compatibility.
CLtL2 says Common Lisp was influenced by Interlisp to some extent; limited design input, not environment compatibility.
CLtL2 says Common Lisp was strongly influenced by Zetalisp, but the fixed PLDB snapshot has no Zetalisp endpoint.
entries.reopenWhen: A fixed Zetalisp record or stable identity source becomes available.

entries.note: Haskell designers history explicitly says Haskell design was strongly influenced by Miranda; scope includes purity, higher order, laziness, static typing and syntax feel.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Lisp as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Common Lisp as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Scheme as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists APL as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Standard ML as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Clean as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
F# author history names C# 1.0 objects/properties/events, C# 3.0 LINQ and C# 7.0 Span as design inputs; no succession or source-compatibility claim.
F# author history does not identify Python as an F# design source; Python is mentioned as an influence on C# 4.0 dynamic.
entries.reopenWhen: An F# design source explicitly names Python as an input for a concrete feature.

entries.note: F# author history says TypeScript was directly influenced by F# and identifies the TypeScript originator’s preceding F# work; design-source claim only.
Clojure official page says it is a member of the Lisp family and inherits code-as-data and macro design; not a claim about every Lisp dialect or source compatibility.
Alice official manual says it is based on Standard ML and lists extensions; not a complete superset or all-program compatibility claim.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists ISWIM as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Backus’s FP as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists ML as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Hope/Hope+ as particularly influential forerunners; overall acknowledged influence only.

Haskell report lists Gofer as an influential forerunner, but Hugs history dates Gofer’s first public release to September 1991. Scope is limited to retrospective/later influence; no claim about Haskell 1.0 in 1990. Chronology warning remains.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Sisal as a particularly influential forerunner; overall acknowledged influence only.
Haskell 98 Report Preface lists Id as a particularly influential forerunner, but the fixed PLDB snapshot has no Id endpoint.

entries.note: Andrew Kelley’s primary introduction explicitly sets “more pragmatic than C” and discusses concrete C comparisons in performance, undefined behavior, error representation, libc and preprocessor policy. Scope is design response/reference, not succession, superset or source compatibility.
Less official About page says Less was originally inspired by Sass and chose a leaner CSS-like syntax; scope is design input, not bidirectional source compatibility or superset.

Official C# specification introduction emphasizes portability and familiarity for programmers already familiar with C/C++, but does not state that C or C++ is a design source for concrete C# language features. Similarity/familiarity is not upgraded to inheritance.
entries.reopenWhen: A Microsoft/C# specification or principal-designer source explicitly names a concrete C or C++ design input.

entries.note: Official C# specification introduction emphasizes portability and familiarity for programmers already familiar with C/C++, but does not state that C or C++ is a design source for concrete C# language features. Similarity/familiarity is not upgraded to inheritance.

entries.note: Crystal official homepage says its syntax is inspired by Ruby and its style guide says heavily inspired; scope is syntax/language-experience input, not Ruby compatibility, dynamic object-model inheritance, or superset.
Elixir official homepage identifies the Erlang VM as the host runtime. This is an implementation/ecosystem relationship, not design inheritance or source compatibility.
Chapel official overview lists C among Chapel's primary influences; recorded as design influence only, not ABI, API, or source compatibility.
Chapel official overview lists Fortran among Chapel's primary influences; recorded as design influence only, not program or runtime compatibility.
Chapel official overview lists Java among Chapel's primary influences; no JVM, succession, or compatibility claim.
Chapel official overview lists Matlab among Chapel's primary influences; recorded as language-design influence only, not toolchain, library, or runtime relationship.
Chapel official overview lists C# among Chapel's primary influences; recorded as design influence only, not .NET/runtime or source compatibility.
Chapel official overview lists CLU among Chapel's primary influences; no claim that individual CLU mechanisms or programs are inherited wholesale.
Chapel official overview lists ML among Chapel's primary influences; no dialect, succession, compatibility, or superset claim.
Chapel official overview lists Modula among Chapel's primary influences; no direct claim about a particular Modula dialect or module-system compatibility.
Chapel official overview lists Scala among Chapel's primary influences; no JVM, object-model, type-system, or source-compatibility claim.
Civet's official Design Philosophy lists Python among the languages it took inspiration from; scope is a listed overall design influence, not syntax, type-system, or output compatibility.

Cobrust's README states it adopts Python ergonomics (indentation, comprehensions, f-strings, decorators, pattern matching); scope is a stated ergonomics orientation, not source-level or runtime compatibility with CPython.
Cobrust's README states it adopts Rust semantics (ownership, Result<T,E>, no GIL, no implicit truthiness); scope is a stated semantic orientation, not toolchain or crate compatibility.
Flare's official project overview lists Python among the languages that inspired its proposed design; scope is a listed overall design inspiration.
Flare's official project overview lists C++ among the languages that inspired its proposed design; scope is a listed overall design inspiration.

HLA's official reference manual states the author chose a syntax very similar to C/C++-class imperative languages and modeled the standard library after C/C++ libraries; scope is stated syntax and standard-library borrowing, not source compatibility.
Please's README states its build language can drop into an imperative language that resembles Python; scope is a stated syntax orientation, not CPython runtime or standard-library compatibility.
MIT PDOS Tick C page states that Tick C ('C) is an extension of ANSI C; scope is the author's extension (superset) classification, not ABI or full dialect compatibility.
Chapel's official overview paper lists its primary influences (C, Modula, Fortran, C++, Java, C#, CLU, Scala, ML, Perl, Matlab) and does not include Python.
